The aim of Job Fair was to bridge the gap between aspiring students and leading companies in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors and provide a valu... view all Events FAQ Q.1 What is Pharmacology, and why is it important in pharmaceutical sciences? Pharmacology is the branch of medicine and biology that studies the effects of drugs on the body. It is essential in pharmaceutical sciences as it helps in understanding how drugs work, their side effects, and their therapeutic uses. Q.2 What are the core subjects covered in the Pharmacology curriculum? The curriculum typically covers topics like drug classification, drug mechanisms, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, toxicology, clinical pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics. Q.3 How does pharmacokinetics differ from pharmacodynamics? Pharmacokinetics involves the study of the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) of drugs in the body, while pharmacodynamics focuses on the effects of drugs on the body, including mechanisms of action. Q.4 What are the career opportunities for Pharmacology graduates? Graduates can pursue careers in research, clinical pharmacology, drug regulatory affairs, drug safety, toxicology, pharmaceutical industry, academic teaching, and healthcare. Q.5 What are the common tools and techniques used in Pharmacology studies? Common tools include animal models, cell cultures, computer simulations, spectrophotometry, chromatography, and various bioassays to study drug effects. Q.6 How is pharmacology related to drug development? Pharmacology plays a key role in the drug development process by providing information on the safety, efficacy, and mechanisms of new drugs, which helps in designing better therapeutics. Q.7 What are the ethical considerations when conducting pharmacology research? Ethical considerations include animal welfare, informed consent in clinical trials, minimizing harm to participants, and ensuring the integrity of research findings. Q.8 What is the role of Pharmacology in personalized medicine? Pharmacology helps in understanding how individual genetic differences affect drug responses, which is crucial for developing personalized treatment plans and optimizing drug therapy. Q.9 What is toxicology, and how is it studied in Pharmacology? Toxicology is the study of the harmful effects of drugs and chemicals on living organisms. It is studied by examining dose-response relationships, organ-specific toxicity, and chronic versus acute effects of substances. Q.10 How does pharmacology contribute to patient care and clinical practice? Pharmacology ensures that healthcare professionals understand the therapeutic uses, dosages, side effects, and interactions of drugs, enabling them to make informed decisions about patient care and medication management. Q.11 What is Pharmacognosy, and why is it important in pharmaceutical sciences? Pharmacognosy is the study of natural products, especially those derived from plants, animals, and microorganisms, used in medicine. It is important in pharmaceutical sciences because it helps in discovering and understanding bioactive compounds that can be developed into therapeutic drugs. Q.12 What are the main branches of Pharmacognosy? The main branches of pharmacognosy include plant pharmacognosy, animal pharmacognosy, microbial pharmacognosy, and the study of marine organisms. These branches focus on different natural sources of bioactive compounds. Q.13 What is the difference between Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry? Pharmacognosy focuses on the medicinal properties, uses, and safety of natural substances, while phytochemistry specifically deals with the chemical constituents of plants and their therapeutic properties. Q.14 How are medicinal plants classified in Pharmacognosy? Medicinal plants are classified based on their therapeutic uses, chemical constituents (e.g., alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenes), and botanical characteristics. They can also be classified into categories like herbs, spices, and other plant-based remedies. Q.15 What methods are used to identify and evaluate medicinal plants? Identification and evaluation of medicinal plants include techniques like macroscopic and microscopic examination, chromatographic methods (e.g., TLC, HPLC), spectroscopy (e.g., UV, IR, NMR), and biological assays for bioactivity. Q.16 What are the therapeutic applications of herbal medicines? Herbal medicines are used in treating a wide range of conditions, including digestive disorders, respiratory diseases, inflammation, pain management, and skin conditions, often as alternative or complementary therapies. Q.17 How are natural products isolated and purified for pharmaceutical use? Natural products are isolated using solvent extraction, distillation, or chromatography. The compounds are then purified through various techniques like recrystallization, column chromatography, and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Q.18 What role does pharmacognosy play in drug discovery and development? Pharmacognosy plays a crucial role in drug discovery by identifying bioactive compounds in natural sources, which can lead to the development of new medications. Many modern drugs are derived from natural products or inspired by them. Q.19 What are the challenges faced in the commercialization of herbal drugs? Challenges include standardization of herbal products, quality control, lack of clinical evidence, regulation and safety concerns, and variability in active compounds due to growing conditions and extraction methods. Q.20 How does pharmacognosy contribute to sustainable medicine and conservation? Pharmacognosy encourages the sustainable use of natural resources, conservation of medicinal plants, and ethical sourcing of raw materials to prevent over-exploitation and ensure the continued availability of bioactive compounds for future generations. Q.21 What is the difference between pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in Pharmaceutics? Pharmacokinetics refers to the study of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME), while pharmacodynamics deals with the study of drug effects and the mechanism of action in the body. Q.22 What are the various types of drug delivery systems covered in Pharmaceutics? Pharmaceutics covers various drug delivery systems such as sustained release, controlled release, transdermal, targeted delivery, and nanoparticles for specific routes of administration. Q.23 How does the pH of the medium affect the dissolution rate of drugs? The pH of the medium can influence the solubility of drugs, especially weak acids and bases, which in turn affects their dissolution rate and bioavailability. Q.24 What is the significance of the bioavailability of a drug in formulation development? Bioavailability refers to the extent and rate at which the active drug enters systemic circulation, affecting the drug's therapeutic efficacy. Formulation strategies aim to optimize bioavailability for effective treatment. Q.25 Explain the concept of 'First Pass Effect' in drug metabolism.? The first-pass effect refers to the metabolism of orally administered drugs by the liver before they enter systemic circulation, which may reduce the drug's effectiveness. Q.26 What is the difference between a solution and a suspension in terms of pharmaceutical A solution is a homogenous mixture where the drug is fully dissolved in a solvent, while a suspension is a heterogeneous mixture where the drug particles are dispersed but not dissolved in the solvent. The program is a full-time undergraduate course with a duration of 3 years. Q.2 What is the admission process for this program at CT University? Admission to the BA with IAS Coaching program at CT University is primarily based on merit in the CT-SET (CT University Scholarship Entrance Test), subject to fulfilling the eligibility criteria. Q.3 How is the IAS coaching integrated into the curriculum? The IAS coaching is a specialized and integrated part of the program, providing targeted training to excel in the IAS examination alongside the general academic studies. Q.4 What career opportunities are available after completing this BA program? Graduates are primarily prepared for the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) exam and other civil services. The comprehensive education also equips them for roles in various government departments, NGOs, research organizations, and further academic pursuits Q.5 Are there any specific facilities or resources at CT University that benefit students of this program? Students have access to general university facilities which include libraries, IT services, and a comprehensive learning environment that supports both academic and competitive exam preparation. Q.6 What is the duration of the B.Sc. (Hons.) Clinical Psychology program at CT University? The B.Sc. (Hons.) Clinical Psychology program at CT University is a 4-year undergraduate course. Q.7 Does the B.Sc. (Hons.) Clinical Psychology program include practical training or internships? Yes, the program typically includes supervised clinical placements or internships in clinical settings, providing hands-on experience in working with individuals facing psychological challenges. Q.8 What kind of practical skills will I develop during this program? Students gain practical skills in assessment, basic intervention strategies, understanding of real-world clinical settings, and ethical considerations in mental health care. Q.9 What are the career prospects after completing a B.Sc. (Hons.) Clinical Psychology from CT University? Graduates are equipped with knowledge and skills to pursue careers in mental health services, counseling roles (under supervision), or further studies in clinical psychology. Many typically pursue an M.Sc. in Clinical Psychology for professional practice. Q.10 What is the duration of the M.Sc. Clinical Psychology program at CT University? The M.Sc. Clinical Psychology program at CT University is a 2-year postgraduate course. Q.11 What advanced topics are covered in the M.Sc. Clinical Psychology curriculum? The curriculum covers advanced topics such as psychopathology, psychotherapy, psychological assessments, and counseling interventions, providing a deep understanding of mental health issues. Q.12 Does the M.Sc. Clinical Psychology program include supervised clinical placements or internships? Yes, a significant component of the M.Sc. Clinical Psychology program involves supervised clinical placements or internships in mental health institutions, hospitals, counseling centers, or private practices. Q.13 What is the duration of the Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program at CT University? The BSW program at CT University is a 3-year undergraduate course. Q.14 What is the core focus or objective of the BSW program at CT University? The BSW program emphasizes the need for self-analysis, moral conduct, and cultural sensitivity in social work practice, aiming to develop human resources for professional social work practice in diverse settings. Q.15 Does the BSW program at CT University include practical fieldwork or internships? Yes, the BSW program includes "Industry Immersion" which typically involves practical training or internships in social organizations, NGOs, government agencies, or rehabilitation centers. Q.16 Does CT University offer support for students seeking BSW-related placements? CT University has a dedicated placement cell that assists students with career guidance, resume building, interview preparation, and connects them with potential employers in the social sector through job fairs and recruitment drives. text:

                now Apply Now University Management System University Management System UMS: AN IN-HOUSE ERP SOLUTION. It sounds like you're describing a University Management System (UMS) that serves as an in-house Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution for a university or educational institution. Such a system typically integrates various functions and processes across the institution to streamline operations and improve efficiency. Here's a breakdown of the key components and features your UMS might include: 1. Learning Management System (LMS): This is a core component for educational institutions. It allows instructors to create and manage courses, upload course materials, track student progress, and facilitate online learning. Students can access course content, submit assignments, and participate in discussions. 2. Student Information System (SIS): This module manages student data, including admissions, registration, grading, attendance, and transcripts. It should provide easy access for both students and administrative staff. 3. eGovernance: This part of the system focuses on the administrative aspects of the university, including finance, HR, and procurement. It might include features for payroll processing, budget management, purchase order tracking, and employee management. 4. Admissions and Enrollment: Streamline the admissions process by allowing applicants to submit applications online, check admission status, and pay fees. Manage enrollment and course registration efficiently. 5. Library Management: Enable library staff to catalog books, manage lending and returns, and provide online access to the library catalog. It may also include features for digital resources and interlibrary loans. 6. Exam Management: Create exam schedules, manage exam registration, and publish results. Ensure security and integrity in the examination process. 7. Communication and Collaboration: Facilitate communication between faculty, staff, and students through email, messaging, and discussion forums. Enable collaboration on projects and assignments. 8. Analytics and Reporting: Provide data analytics and reporting tools to help administrators make informed decisions. Generate reports on student performance, financial data, and other key metrics. 9. Security and Access Control: Implement robust security measures to protect sensitive data. Ensure role-based access control to restrict information based on user roles and permissions. 10. Mobile Accessibility: Offer a mobile-friendly interface or dedicated mobile apps to allow stakeholders to access information and perform tasks on the go. 11. Integration: Integrate with external systems, such as financial software, email systems, and external databases, to ensure seamless data flow and information exchange. 12. Scalability: Design the system to accommodate growth in terms of users, courses, and data volume. 13. User Support and Training: Provide comprehensive user support and training materials to help users make the most of the system. 14. Customization: Allow for customization to adapt the system to the specific needs and workflows of the institution. 15. Data Backup and Recovery: Implement regular data backups and a disaster recovery plan to safeguard critical data. 16. Regulatory Compliance: Ensure the system complies with relevant regulations and standards in education and data privacy. Creating an in-house ERP solution is a significant undertaking and requires careful planning, development, and ongoing maintenance. It's essential to involve key stakeholders, including administrators, faculty, and IT experts, in the design and implementation process to ensure that the UMS meets the unique needs of your institution. Additionally, stay updated with emerging technologies and trends in education to continually enhance and evolve your UMS. LMS: A SYSTEM TO MANAGE ACADEMIC FUNCTIONS. MAJOR MODULES OF LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (LMS) LMS: A SYSTEM TO MANAGE ACADEMIC FUNCTIONS. A Learning Management System (LMS) designed to manage academic functions within a university plays a crucial role in streamlining various educational activities. Here's a more detailed overview of how such an LMS can benefit academic institutions: 1. Academic Record Management: An LMS serves as a central repository for academic records, making it easy to access information related to students, courses, and academic performance. This includes attendance records, assignment submissions, and examination results. 2. Attendance Tracking: The LMS can automate the process of recording student attendance. Faculty members can take attendance digitally, and the system can generate attendance reports for students and administrators. 3. Assignment Management: Faculty members can use the LMS to upload assignments, set due dates, and collect submissions electronically. This simplifies the assignment submission process for students and allows instructors to grade assignments online. 4. Course Materials and Resources: The LMS provides a platform for instructors to upload course materials such as lecture notes, slides, reading materials, and multimedia content. Students can access these resources at their convenience. 5. Grading and Assessment: The LMS can facilitate grading and assessment by allowing instructors to input grades, calculate final grades, and provide feedback to students. It can also generate grade reports for students and academic administrators. 6. Discussion Forums and Collaboration: An LMS often includes discussion forums and collaboration tools that enable students and instructors to engage in online discussions, group projects, and collaborative activities related to the course. 7. Course Scheduling: It can help in scheduling classes and managing course timetables. Students can view their course schedules, including dates, times, and locations. 8. Student Communication: The LMS can facilitate communication between students and instructors through messaging systems, announcements, and email notifications. 9. Assessment Tools: Some LMS platforms offer built-in assessment and quiz tools, allowing instructors to create and administer quizzes and assessments digitally. 10. Analytics and Reporting: The system can generate analytics and reports on student performance, attendance trends, and course completion rates, providing valuable insights for academic administrators. 11. Accessibility: A well-designed LMS should be accessible to students with disabilities, ensuring equal access to educational resources and materials. 12. Security and Data Privacy: Protecting sensitive academic data is crucial. The LMS should have robust security measures in place to safeguard student and faculty information. 13. Integration: Integration with other university systems, such as the Student Information System (SIS) and library databases, can provide a seamless experience for users and reduce data redundancy. 14. Mobile Compatibility: Many students and faculty members use mobile devices, so ensuring that the LMS is mobile-responsive or has dedicated mobile apps can enhance accessibility. 15. User Support and Training: Offer user support and training resources to help both students and instructors effectively navigate and use the LMS. 16. Customization: Allow for customization to adapt the LMS to the unique needs and workflows of the university. In summary, an LMS designed to manage academic functions is a versatile and powerful tool for educational institutions. It not only helps streamline administrative processes but also enhances the learning experience for students and instructors by providing a centralized platform for communication, resource sharing, and assessment. Since its inception, the NCC has played a pivotal role in student development, offering a range of activities that help students grow both personally and professionally. The NCC program at CT University equips cadets with skills and experiences that are beneficial not only for their future careers but also for their personal growth. The department is an integral part of the university's commitment to producing well-rounded, disciplined, and skilled individuals who can contribute meaningfully to society. FSFS Vacancies The NCC department at CT University has been allocated 160 FSFS (Full Time Service Faculty) vacancies by the 3 Punjab Battalion NCC, Ludhiana, allowing cadets to gain valuable exposure and experience in their training. 2. Firing Range CT University features a 50-meter firing range on campus, providing cadets with regular firing practice as part of their military training. This facility helps cadets improve their shooting accuracy and skills, an essential aspect of NCC training. 3. Camps and Training NCC cadets at CT University have the opportunity to participate in various National, State, and Adventure Camps, organized by the NCC and the Indian Army. These camps provide practical military and tactical training, along with valuable exposure to different environments and scenarios. Additionally, cadets attend **Army Attachment Camps**, which give them hands-on experience in military operations and a closer look at the functioning of the armed forces. 4.                 now Apply Now Orientation Ambassadors Orientation Ambassadors Orientation Ambassadors in a university play a crucial role in welcoming and assisting new students, both freshmen and transfer students, during their transition to university life. These ambassadors are typically current students who are knowledgeable about campus resources, services, and university culture. Their primary objective is to help new students acclimate to the university environment, build a sense of belonging, and answer any questions or concerns that the newcomers may have. The responsibilities of Orientation Ambassadors often include: 1. Welcoming and Orientation: Greet new students and their families on arrival and provide them with an initial orientation to the campus, including information about key locations, services, and resources. 2. Campus Tours: Conduct campus tours to familiarize new students with important places, such as academic buildings, libraries, student centers, and dining facilities. 3. Information Sessions: Host informational sessions on topics such as academic programs, university policies, financial aid, and extracurricular activities. 4. Peer Support: Offer emotional and academic support to new students, addressing concerns and connecting them with appropriate resources. 5. Social Integration: Organize and participate in social events, icebreakers, and group activities to help new students connect with their peers and build a sense of community. 6. Resource Guidance: Assist students in accessing important resources, such as the university website, course registration system, and library services. 7. Answering Questions: Be available to answer questions from new students about academic life, campus culture, and available support services. 8. Safety and Emergency Procedures: Educate students about safety procedures and emergency protocols on campus. 9. Mentorship: Provide mentorship and guidance to new students throughout their first semester or year, helping them adjust to university life. 10. Crisis Management: Be trained to handle or report any crisis situations or concerns that may arise among new students. 11. Feedback Collection: Gather feedback from new students about their orientation experience and share this information with the university administration to improve future orientations. 12. Teamwork: Collaborate with other Orientation Ambassadors and university staff to ensure a smooth transition process. Benefits Requirements Benefits Benefits Orientation Ambassadors in a university play a crucial role in welcoming and assisting new students during their transition to campus life. These ambassadors are typically current students who have experience with the university and can help newcomers navigate various aspects of university life, including academic, social, and administrative matters. The benefits of having Benefits Orientation Ambassadors include: Smooth Transition: New students often face challenges in adjusting to university life. Orientation Ambassadors can help ease this transition by providing guidance and information on campus resources, facilities, and services. Personalized Guidance: Ambassadors can offer personalized assistance, answering questions and addressing concerns based on their own experiences, making new students feel more comfortable and supported. First-Hand Insights: Ambassadors can share their own experiences, including tips and advice on class schedules, professors, extracurricular activities, and more, giving newcomers a practical understanding of university life. Enhanced Engagement: Orientation Ambassadors can promote student involvement in campus activities, clubs, and organizations. Their enthusiasm can inspire new students to participate in the university community. Improved Retention: By helping students integrate into the campus community and connecting them with resources, Ambassadors can contribute to higher retention rates. Students who feel engaged and supported are more likely to stay and succeed. Requirements Orientation Ambassadors in a university play a crucial role in welcoming and assisting new students, whether they are incoming freshmen, transfer students, or international students. They help ease the transition to university life, provide information, and create a positive and inclusive atmosphere during orientation programs. Here are the requirements and characteristics for Orientation Ambassadors in a university: Current Student Status: Orientation Ambassadors should be current students of the university. They need to have experience and familiarity with campus life and resources. Good Academic Standing: Ambassadors should maintain good academic standing to serve as role models for new students.                 now Apply Now About IQAC ABOUT INTERNAL QUALITY ASSURANCE CELL (IQAC) IQAC – VISION To ensure quality culture as the prime concern for the Higher Education Institutions through institutionalizing and internalizing all the initiatives taken with internal and external support. OBJECTIVE To develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic action to improve the academic and administrative performance of the institution. To promote measures for institutional functioning towards quality enhancement through internalization of quality culture and institutionalization of best practices. STRATEGIES Ensuring timely, efficient and progressive performance of academic, administrative and financial tasks; The Relevance and quality of academic/research programmes; Equitable access to and affordability of academic programmes for various sections of society; Optimization and integration of modern methods of teaching and learning; The credibility of assessment and evaluation process; Ensuring the adequacy, maintenance and proper allocation of support structure and services; Sharing of research findings and networking with other institutions in India and abroad. FUNCTIONS Development and application of quality benchmarks/parameters for various academic and administrative activities of the institution; Facilitating the creation of a learner-centric environment conducive to quality education and faculty maturation to adopt the required knowledge and technology for participatory teaching and learning process; Collection and analysis of feedback from all stakeholders on quality-related institutional processes; Dissemination of information on various quality parameters to all stakeholders; BENEFITS Ensure clarity and focus in institutional functioning towards quality enhancement; Ensure internalization of the quality culture; Ensure enhancement and coordination among various activities of the institution and institutionalize all good practices; Provide a sound basis for decision-making to improve institutional functioning; Act as a dynamic system for quality changes in HEIs; Build an organised methodology of documentation and internal communication. As per National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) guidelines every accredited institution should establish an Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) as a post-accreditation quality sustenance measure. Since quality enhancement is a continuous process, the IQAC becomes a part of the institution’s system and works towards the realization of the goals of quality enhancement and sustenance.  The prime task of the IQAC is to develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic improvement in the overall performance of institutions. The CT University, established in 2016 has proactively developed the need-based system of governance, curriculum delivery, and research component and outreach mechanism.                 now Apply Now Composition The Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) is a crucial component of an educational institution's quality assurance system. It plays a significant role in ensuring and enhancing the quality of education and services provided by the institution. Composing the IQAC involves selecting members who can contribute effectively to this mission. Here's a typical composition for an IQAC: 1. Chairperson: The head of the institution, like the Principal or Director, usually serves as the Chairperson of the IQAC. They provide leadership and guidance. 2. Coordinators: The IQAC typically has one or more coordinators who are responsible for day-to-day operations and communication. These individuals often have a background in educational administration or quality management. 3. Teachers: Faculty members from various departments or disciplines are an essential part of the IQAC. They can provide valuable insights into curriculum development, teaching methodologies, and student feedback. 4. Administrative Staff: Staff members from the administrative side, like the Registrar or the Examination Controller, are included. They offer a perspective on administrative processes and their impact on quality. 5. Students: It's essential to have student representation to understand their perspective and concerns regarding the quality of education. Students can bring fresh ideas and insights. 6. Alumni: Alumni can provide feedback on the institution's effectiveness in preparing students for the real world. They can also contribute to the development of the institution's goals. 7. External Experts: Inviting external experts, preferably from other reputable institutions, industry professionals, or education experts, can provide an unbiased view of the institution's quality and suggest improvements. 8. Local Society Representatives: Including individuals from the local community or relevant government bodies can help ensure the institution's programs align with community needs and government policies. 9. Quality Assurance Experts: If available, individuals with expertise in quality assurance and accreditation processes can be valuable additions to the IQAC. 10. Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) Representatives: In some cases, it might be beneficial to involve representatives from NGOs that work in the field of education, as they can provide a different perspective and collaborate on social responsibility initiatives. 11. Industry Representatives: Including professionals from industries related to the institution's academic programs can help in curriculum development and ensuring that graduates are industry-ready. 12. Librarian: The librarian can contribute to ensuring the availability of up-to-date learning resources and information. 13. IT Expert: An IT expert can assist in incorporating technology for educational and administrative purposes. 14. Public Relations Officer (PRO): The PRO can help with communication and outreach to the wider public and media. 15. Legal Advisor: If the institution has a legal advisor, their input can be crucial for ensuring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. 16. Environmental and Sustainability Officer: As environmental concerns become more critical, having a sustainability officer on the IQAC can help ensure the institution's policies align with environmental responsibility.                     qualifying with qualifying marks as 50%. The syllabus of the Entrance Test shall consist of 50% of
                    research methodology and 50% shall be subject specific. The Entrance Test shall be conducted at the
                    University. Stage II (Interview): University shall organize an
                    interview where the successful candidates in stage I are required to discuss their research
                    interest/area through a presentation before a duly constituted Department Research Committee. The
                    interview shall also consider whether: The candidate possesses the competence for the proposed research; The research work can be suitably undertaken at the Institution/College; The proposed area of research can contribute to new/additional knowledge. Selection Criteria Stage wise (Entrance and Interview) and Discipline/Program
                wise merit list will be prepared. Candidates successful in Entrance test (Stage I) will be called for
                interview (Stage II). The final selection for admission in Ph.D. will be based on the performance in the
                Interview subject to scoring minimum marks. Eligibility (Any one of the following) Master's degree or a professional degree declared equivalent to the
                    Master's degree by the corresponding statutory body, with at least 55% marks in aggregate or its
                    equivalent grade B in UGC 7-point scale (or an equivalent grade in a point scale wherever grading
                    system is followed) or an equivalent degree from a foreign educational institution accredited by an
                    Assessment and Accreditation Agency which is approved, recognised by an authority, established or
                    incorporated under a law in its home country or any other statutory authority in that country for
                    the purpose of assessing or assuring quality and standards of educational institutions. A relaxation of 5% of marks, 55% to 50%, or an equivalent relaxation of
                    grade, may be allowed for those belonging to SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer)/Differently-Abled and
                    other categories of candidates as per decision of the UGC from time to time, or for those who had
                    obtained their Master's degree prior to 19th September, 1991. The eligibility marks of 55% (or an
                    equivalent grade in a point scale wherever grading system is followed) and the relaxation of 5% to
                    the categories mentioned above are permissible based only on the qualifying marks without including
                    the grace mark procedures. Candidates who have cleared the M.Phil. Course work with at least 55%
                    marks in aggregate or its equivalent grade B in UGC 7- point scale (or an equivalent grade in a
                    point scale wherever grading system is followed). A person who’s M.Phil. Thesis has been evaluated
                    and the viva voce is pending may be admitted provisionally to Ph.D. Programme. Candidates possessing a Degree considered equivalent to M.Phil. Degree
                    of an Indian Institution, from a Foreign Educational Institution accredited by an Accreditation and
                    Assessment Agency which is approved, recognized or authorized by an authority, established or
                    incorporated under a law in its home country or any other statutory authority in that country for
                    the purpose of accessing, accrediting or assuring quality and standards of educational institutions,
                    shall be eligible for admission to Ph.D. Programme. Exemption from Entrance Test: Candidates who qualify UGC-NET (including JRF)/UGC-CSIR NET (including
                    JRF)/SLET/GATE/teacher fellowship holder or have passed M.Phil. Programme (regular mode only). Course work: A student is required to undertake a course work for one semester. Attendance in course work: The attendance for course work shall be mandatory as per the University’s
                    attendance rules as defined in the Academic and Examination rules for regular Programmes shall be
                    applicable. Exemption in Course Work: Candidates already holding M. Phil. Degree (regular mode) and admitted to
                    the Ph.D. Programme, or those who have already completed the course work in M.Phil. and have been

title: International Student Information & Guidelines | CT University
text:
Apply Now Programmes Virtual Tour CT-SET 2026 Ph.D Admissions Open 2026-27 Apply
                now Apply Now Student Information GUIDELINES FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS Comprehensive pre-departure, visa regulations, and post-arrival guidelines for CT
            University, Punjab, India. GUIDELINES FOR VISA APPLICATION Foreign Nationals desirous of coming into India are required to possess a
                        valid passport of their country and a valid Indian Visa. The only exceptions are nationals of
                        Nepal and Bhutan who can enter India without a visa. (Note: Nepalese nationals need a visa if
                        entering India from China). To study in India it is mandatory for an international student to procure
                        an Indian Student Visa. Visas can be applied for in person or by post (in certain High
                        Commissions/Embassies, it is responsibility of the student to check with particular embassy on
                        postal visa application) to the High Commission of India based in the country from where the
                        candidate intends to depart for India. Applicant need to mention the name of the Institute while applying for the
                        visa, which is then mentioned on the visa. International students taking admission at CT University should make sure
                        that the Student visa is endorsed to CT University by the visa issuing authority. A request for change of university or institution subsequently made cannot
                        be considered. In this case you would be required to go back to your home country and apply for
                        a new visa. Also, if you have entered India on basis of documents provided by the CT
                        University then it is your responsibility to ensure that you directly join and report to the CT
                        University. The Visa endorsed on the name of the University or obtained on the basis of CT
                        University documents cannot be used for any other purpose like employment , admission to any
                        other university/college/institute/academy etc or for non-regular (distance/online) mode of
                        education. After reaching the university students have to get the visa verified by
                        the University and have to deposit a copy of the valid visa. It is the responsibility of the student to ensure that throughout his/her
                        study period student is on valid visa. In case the initial visa is not endorsed for the complete duration of the
                        program or student has to extend the stay because he/she is not able to complete the program in
                        the stipulated time then the student should apply for the extension of the visa before visa
                        expires. It is the responsibility of the student to ensure that visa should be
                        applied well in advance and time. It generally takes 3-8 weeks to get the Indian Visa thus it is
                        advisable to apply for the visa accordingly and consult the Indian High Commission/Embassy if
                        required. In case a student reports to the university late because of the Visa
                        /Tickets Availability or any other personal issue, no relaxation related to attendance or any
                        favor for completing the assignment, submitting the missed assignments, sitting for the missed
                        examination(s), relaxation in the marks etc. will be given. Students joining the university after the prescribed time period may be
                        denied admission. In such cases the fees etc. deposited by the applicant would be forfeited and
                        further no claim for the expense made for the travelling, visa or any other expense made or
                        hardship suffered by the student will be entertained. Even, after joining the university if the student leaves the country then
                        it is the responsibility of the student to report back at the university on time. It some cases
                        where visa extension is required it is the responsibility of the student to ensure to get the
                        valid visa extension on time. In case student reports to the university late because of the Visa
                        / Tickets Availability or any other personal issue then student will not be provided any
                        relaxation related to attendance, extra time to complete the assignments, opportunity to submit
                        the missed assignments, opportunity to sit for the missed examination(s), relaxation in the
                        marks etc. In case student is expelled from the university or the student decides to
                        leave the program then an affidavit has to be submitted to the university that he/she will leave
                        India immediately and will not use visa issued on the basis of CT University documents to stay
                        in India. University may debar the student to continue attending classes or staying
                        in the university residential facility if student does not maintain a valid visa / FRRO or does
                        not follow any guidelines issued by the Govt. of India / Govt. of Punjab/ University
                        Administration/ any other authority from time to time. For loss of attendance / academics or any expenditure so occurred because
                        of such action by the university, the student himself will be responsible and no relaxation or
                        benefit may be provided in such cases and all expenditure has to be borne by the student. PRE-DEPARTURE GUIDELINES The following points will give you a quick preview of what all should be taken care of before you
                    look forward to depart from your home country: Ensure that you obtain visa from Indian Embassy/ High Commission. Also assure that you meet Medical fitness standard before you leave your
                        country. Also ensure that you have taken all the required vaccinations (Typhoid
                        Vaccine, Hepatitis Vaccine), to avoid medical complications while you are in India(though it is
                        not mandatory). If there are certain medicines that you are supposed to consume due to any
                        medical reason prescribed by a doctor please carry them along. It is also suggested to carry the
                        prescription of that medicine for any further reference. Request and register with the University International Office for the pick
                        service from the Airport at least two weeks prior to arrival and provide the complete details of
                        flight. Also ensure that you bring the letter of admission issued by the
                        University. Make sure that you carry the originals, copies of your
                        certificates/degrees and 10 passport size photographs. Ensure that your fee has been received by the University and you should
                        carry the fee receipt. You can carry all your money in form of Travellers Cheques & USD in
                        cash which can be easily redeemed at the airport as well as a number of foreign exchange offices
                        and banks. Keep all the valuables, important documents (Passport, Visa papers) in the
                        Cabin baggage, to avoid the possibility of their getting misplaced during transit. Keep all the contact phone numbers handy in case of need. Temperature ranges between 35 – 45 degree Celsius during summers and 5 –
                        20 degree Celsius during winters. Here the winter season starts around October or November so
                        the warm material (blankets, quilts, woolens, etc) must be brought accordingly. Whilst everything is available in India, however try to get all that you
                        would require during the initial few days. All the essentials can be availed from the University
                        tuck shops. The electric standard in India works on 240 V. So, ensure that you have an
                        adapter for your mobile or laptop if it operates on a different voltage in your country. Also
                        the electric sockets are 2 or 3 pin so ensure that you carry a converter in case required. POST ARRIVAL GUIDELINES On your arrival in India, there are certain points that you should keep in mind. Customs Formalities: Foreign students in India are generally required to make an oral baggage declaration of the
                    possession of baggage and foreign currency as soon as they land in India. Under this they are also required to obtain the Currency Declaration Form from the Customs. The
                    students should also fill in the Disembarkation Card (Arrival card) handed over to them by the
                    airline during the course of the flight. Clearance: There are two channels for clearance: Green Channel: For passengers not in possession of any
                        dutiable articles or unaccompanied baggage. Red Channel: For passengers in possession of dutiable
                        articles or unaccompanied baggage or high value articles. High value articles are to be entered
                        on the tourist Baggage Re-Export Form. CT University arranges for pick-up facility for the international students from Delhi, Chandigarh or
                    Amritsar Airport on the student request. To avail this facility a student must request and register
                    for the service at least two weeks prior to arrival and provide the complete details of flight. Also
                    pick-up facility is offered to all international students from Ludhiana railway station or bus
                    terminals, for which prior information and registration is mandatory. Once an international student
                    is settled, he/she should complete the following formalities and paperwork: Registration: All international students
                        must register themselves with the
                        International Office of CT University. Admission Formalities: The International Office of the University should be
                    contacted to take care of the admission formalities. Medical Examination and HIV
                        Test All international students coming to India for studies need to go through a
                    medical test for HIV. The Foreigner's Regional Registration Office (FRRO) requires this test as a
                    pre-requisite for obtaining the residence permit form. Registration with FRRO: All International students who have come to study in India
                    need to get themselves in The Foreigner's Regional Registration Office (FRRO) within 14 days of
                    arrival in India (not applicable in the case of Bhutanese and Nepalese students). The University's
                    International Office helps and guides the students in the registration. Documents Checklist for Reporting: Student should be in possession of following things while reporting to International Affairs office
                    in Block B, Ist Floor, CT University, Ferozepur Road, Ludhiana, Punjab, India: Valid Passport with arrival stamp Copy of valid visa endorsed in the name of CT University C Form, In case a student is residing outside the campus Bank statement / Banking details Valid email address and valid contact number Original Academic Documents Passport Photographs Acceptance Letter of the university Bonafide Certificate Enquire Now Subscribe for the
                    Newsletters

title: CT University International Campus Life | Live, Learn and Grow
text:
Apply Now Programmes Virtual Tour CT-SET 2026 Ph.D Admissions Open 2026-27 Apply
                now Apply Now Campus Life Campus Life Vibrant Campus Life &
            Cultural Diversity Where 40 Countries Share One Campus. Campus life for international students at CT University is genuinely
                diverse — not just on paper. Students from over 40+ countries study
                here, and that mix changes everyday life in quiet ways: lunch
                conversations in three languages, cultural fests that feel authentic,
                friendships that don't fit easy categories. Outside the classroom, there's real activity. CT University runs 13+
                    student clubs covering technology, entrepreneurship, dance, sports, and
                more. International students here don't sit on the sidelines — many end
                up leading clubs by their second semester. Settling into a new country mid-degree is hard, and the campus is set up
                with that in mind. Resident faculty live on-site , student support runs
                beyond university hours, and the existing international community tends
                to make the transition feel less like starting over. Cultural Events Celebrate rich heritage with international food fests, traditional performances, and cultural
                        exchange evenings hosted right on campus. View The
                        Events Festivals Experience cross-cultural celebrations and festive seasons, bringing together students and
                        faculty from over 40+ countries. View The
                        Events Annual Fest CT University's flagship annual mega fest featuring dynamic inter-university competitions,
                        celebrity nights, and student showcases. View The
                        Events Clubs & Organizations Find Your People. Then Lead Them. The Department of Student Welfare (DSW) at CT University runs 13+
                    student clubs — designed for students who want to do more than just
                attend. The range covers a lot of ground. Technical and engineering clubs,
                entrepreneurship groups working on live projects, sports teams competing
                at intercollegiate level, dance and music organizations, health and
                wellness initiatives, and a student government that actually advocates
                for the student body. Most students find something that fits within the
                first few weeks. Joining a club means taking on real responsibility: organizing events,
                managing budgets, collaborating across different schools. That
                experience shows up on a resume — but most students will tell you the
                pressure and people skills matter more. Details Sports & Physical Well-being Train Seriously. Compete Harder. Sports at CT University are treated as a real part of university life,
                not a wellness checkbox. The facilities back that up: an athletic track,
                an Olympic-sized swimming pool , a football ground, basketball courts,
                and a dedicated martial arts training center — maintained for regular
                student use, not just events. Students train under qualified coaches and compete off-campus at North
                    Zone Inter-University and All-India Inter-University level. The
                nine-school Inter-School games give students structured competition
                throughout the year. For national-level athletes, sports scholarships are available — worth
                checking eligibility before you enroll. The training schedules,
                coaching, and infrastructure are built for students who want to take it
                seriously. Details Hostel Life & Cafeteria A Good Room Makes a Real Difference. Where you live shapes your university experience more than you'd expect.
                CT University hostels are separate for boys and girls, well-maintained,
                and staffed by resident faculty who live on-site — not just listed as
                emergency contacts. The day-to-day setup covers what matters: 24/7 Wi-Fi , uninterrupted
                power, solar geysers, and round-the-clock security with CCTV coverage.
                Common spaces include a gym, music rooms, a reading room with
                international newspapers, and an in-house salon. Meals are served through the attached mess and a night cafeteria. Menus
                are designed with a mixed student population in mind — dietary variety
                is real, not just stated. Hostel-level volleyball and basketball
                    courts are available for downtime. Resident faculty are available after hours for academic support and
                personal guidance. For international students navigating a new country,
                that on-site presence matters more than it sounds. Details Campus Life Gallery A glimpse into everyday moments, cultural celebrations, and life on campus. ‹ › Enquire Now Subscribe for the

HSS Senior Secondary candidates shall be treated at par with other Senior Secondary candidates for applicable scholarships, financial assistance, fee concessions and other institutional or Government benefits. title: CTU STUDENT WINS SILVER AT WAF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP 2026 - CT University
text:
CTU STUDENT WINS SILVER AT WAF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP 2026 Tuesday, 03 November 2026 1 / 3 View Full Image Event Photo Gallery
                                    (3) About This Event Bringing international recognition and sporting glory to CT University, its talented armwrestling athlete, Harkomal Singh Gill, has won a prestigious Silver Medal at the WAF World Armwrestling Championship 2026, held in Delhi, India. Competing in the highly competitive 85 kg Youth Category, Harkomal demonstrated exceptional strength, determination, discipline and sporting excellence to secure his place on the international podium. The championship witnessed an impressive global participation, bringing together more than 1,700 athletes from over 60 countries, making it a significant international platform for armwrestling talent. Competing against some of the finest young athletes from across the world, Harkomal’s remarkable performance reflects his dedication towards the sport and his ability to excel at the highest level of international competition. His achievement marks another proud milestone for CT University, reinforcing the institution’s growing presence in competitive sports and its commitment to providing students with opportunities to showcase their talent on national and international platforms. The silver medal is not only a personal accomplishment for Harkomal but also a moment of immense pride for the university fraternity. Congratulating the young athlete, Chancellor, Sd. Charanjit Singh Channi, said, “Harkomal Singh Gill’s achievement at the World Armwrestling Championship is a matter of immense pride for the entire CT University family. Winning a silver medal while competing against athletes from more than 60 countries reflects his dedication, perseverance and determination. Such accomplishments inspire other students to pursue their aspirations with confidence and remind us that consistent hard work and the right opportunities can take young talent to international heights. We congratulate Harkomal and wish him many more milestones in his sporting journey.” Pro Chancellor, Dr. Manbir Singh, congratulated Harkomal and stated, “At CT University, we strongly believe that education goes beyond classrooms, and sports play an equally important role in shaping confident, disciplined and resilient individuals. Harkomal’s international achievement is a testament to the talent nurtured at our university and the importance of encouraging students to pursue excellence in their chosen fields. This silver medal is a proud moment for us, and we hope his success motivates more students to participate in competitive sports and represent the university at prestigious international events.” The university also acknowledged the dedicated efforts and support of Director, Department of Student Welfare (DSW), Er. Davinder Singh, and Sports Head, Gurdeep Singh, whose continuous guidance, encouragement and support played an important role in facilitating the university’s sporting talent. Their efforts towards promoting sports culture, providing opportunities to athletes and encouraging participation in competitive platforms remain instrumental in strengthening the university’s sports ecosystem. With this remarkable international achievement, CT University continues to celebrate the spirit of excellence, perseverance and ambition, encouraging its students to push boundaries, compete globally and bring laurels to the institution. Harkomal Singh Gill’s silver medal is more than a sporting victory; it is a reflection of the determination and global aspirations that define the CT University spirit. Back to All Events

title: SAAE-2026 | 9th Annual Conference
text:
Society for Alternatives to Animal Experiments (SAAE - India) 9 th Annual
            Conference “Ethical and Technology-Driven Alternatives to Animal Experiments” Dates: 26–28 November 2026 Organized by: School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, CT University, Ludhiana, Punjab, India Register Online (Google Form) Download Brochure (PDF) About the Conference The previous conferences were conducted successfully by SAAE - India at various organizations
            (CSIR-Hyderabad, AMU-Aligarh, University of Kerala-Trivandrum, DPSRU-New Delhi, G.N. Khalsa College-Mumbai
            and Jamia Hamdard University-New Delhi). It is a proud moment for School of Pharmaceutical sciences, CT
            University to organize the 9th Annual Conference of SAAE - India which is envisioned as a dynamic platform
            dedicated to strengthening and advancing the principles of the 3Rs—Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement—by
            fostering ethical, scientifically robust, and human-relevant alternatives to traditional animal-based
            research. Centered on innovation and responsibility, the conference will highlight the rapid evolution of New Approach
            Methodologies (NAMs), including in vitro systems, organ-on-chip technologies, computational modeling,
            artificial intelligence, and other digital innovations that are reshaping the landscape of biomedical
            research, toxicology, pharmacology, and life science education. By bringing together a diverse and interdisciplinary community of researchers, academicians, industry
            leaders, educators, regulators, and policymakers, the conference aims to encourage meaningful dialogue,
            knowledge exchange, and collaborative problem-solving across sectors. Discussions will focus on the
            scientific validation, regulatory acceptance, and practical implementation of non-animal models, as well as
            strategies to integrate these approaches into research pipelines, safety assessment frameworks, and
            educational curricula. The event will also emphasize capacity building, skill development, and policy alignment to accelerate the
            adoption of humane, efficient, and predictive research methodologies. Through keynote lectures, panel
            discussions, and interactive sessions, the conference seeks to bridge gaps between science, regulation, and
            ethics, ultimately supporting the global transition toward more sustainable, innovative, and human-relevant
            research practices that align with societal expectations and advance both scientific excellence and animal
            welfare. Conference Highlights Focused on 3Rs: Replacement, Reduction, Refinement in animal research. Cutting-Edge Technologies: Covers NAMs, organ-on-chip, AI, in silico models, organoids,
                and human-centric toxicology. Prestigious Expert Network: Strong expert network from ICMR, DBT, NIPER, AIIMS, CSIR,
                Harvard, and TU Berlin. Ethical & Technology-Driven: Promotes ethical, human-relevant, and technology-driven
                biomedical research. Global Sessions: Includes international keynote lectures, oral/poster presentations,
                and policy panels. title: CT University Celebrates Diwali with Dhanak 2026 – The Grand Diwali Carnival - CT University
text:
CT University Celebrates Diwali with Dhanak 2026 – The Grand Diwali Carnival Friday, 30 October 2026 1 / 9 View Full Image Event Photo Gallery
                                    (9) About This Event CT University, Ludhiana, celebrated Dhanak 2026 – The Grand Diwali Carnival with immense enthusiasm, festive spirit and a vibrant display of cultural diversity, creativity and student talent. Organised by the Division of Student Welfare (DSW), the carnival brought together students and faculty members for a memorable celebration of India’s rich cultural heritage, artistic expression and the spirit of togetherness. The campus was transformed into a lively festive space, reflecting the colours, traditions and excitement associated with Diwali. The event was graced by the special presence of Vice Chairman Harpreet Singh, Vice Chancellor Dr. Nitin Tandon, Registrar Sanjay Khanduri and Director, DSW, Er. Davinder Singh, whose presence encouraged the students and added significance to the celebrations. Their participation reflected the university’s commitment to providing students with opportunities to explore their interests, showcase their abilities and engage in activities beyond academics. The carnival featured a diverse range of competitions and activities across three major segments: Cultural, Literary and Science, and Fine Arts. The cultural segment included Tune to Dance, Indian Heritage Dance and CT Sur Sartaj, providing students with a platform to showcase their artistic abilities and celebrate India’s cultural traditions. The Literary and Science segment featured Project Display, Prashnottari Quiz, Just Debate, Poetry, Extempore and Declamation, encouraging intellectual engagement, scientific curiosity, critical thinking and effective communication. The Fine Arts segment witnessed creative participation through activities such as Rangoli, Poster Making, Paint Your Imagination, Cartooning, Clay Modelling and Face Painting. These activities offered students an opportunity to express their imagination through colours, designs and artistic creations. Adding to the festive atmosphere, the carnival also featured food stalls, dance and music, along with cultural performances that brought the university community together in celebration. Speaking on the occasion, Chancellor Sardar Charanjit Singh Channi said, “At CT University, we believe that education extends beyond classrooms and textbooks. Platforms such as Dhanak provide students with opportunities to discover their talents, celebrate their cultural roots and develop confidence through active participation. Such celebrations strengthen the values of unity, creativity and mutual respect while preparing students to become confident individuals with a broader outlook towards life.” Pro-Chancellor Dr. Manbir Singh remarked, “Dhanak 2026 reflects the vibrant spirit, creativity and enthusiasm of our university community. Cultural and artistic platforms play an important role in nurturing students’ personalities, encouraging teamwork and developing a sense of belonging. We remain committed to creating an enriching campus environment where every student gets the opportunity to explore their potential, express themselves and create meaningful memories.” The celebration concluded on a high note, with students and faculty members participating enthusiastically and making Dhanak 2026 a memorable occasion. The carnival once again highlighted CT University’s commitment to holistic education, cultural appreciation and the all-round development of its students. Back to All Events

title: CT University Partners with Quick Heal Academy - CT University
text:
CT University Partners with Quick Heal Academy Friday, 23 October 2026 1 / 3 View Full Image Event Photo Gallery
                                    (3) About This Event Collaboration Offers 24 Industry-Oriented Courses CompTIA Certification Pathways to Boost Cybersecurity Skills Ludhiana: CT University has entered into an industry–academia collaboration with Quick Heal Academy (QHA), a division of Quick Heal Technologies Limited, headquartered in Pune, Maharashtra, to strengthen cybersecurity education and equip students with industry-relevant skills. With over three decades of research and development in computer and network security solutions, Quick Heal Technologies Limited is among India’s leading IT security solutions companies. The collaboration aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry expectations by integrating practical cybersecurity education, hands-on training and professional certification pathways into university programmes. Under this initiative, 14 industry-oriented courses will be offered to B.Tech students and 10 courses to BCA students. Additionally, four B.Tech courses and two BCA courses will be mapped with globally recognised CompTIA certification pathways. The initiative will help students strengthen their technical competencies, gain industry exposure and develop future-ready skills for emerging opportunities in cybersecurity and digital security. Sardar Charanjit Singh Channi, Chancellor, CT University, said, “In today’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, cybersecurity has become a critical priority across industries. Our collaboration with Quick Heal Academy reflects our commitment to providing students with education that goes beyond textbooks and prepares them for real-world challenges. By bringing industry expertise into the academic ecosystem, we aim to nurture skilled, confident and responsible professionals who can contribute meaningfully to the digital future.” He further added, “At CT University, we believe that strong industry partnerships are essential to building a future-ready generation. Initiatives such as this provide students with opportunities to develop practical expertise, understand global industry standards and explore emerging career pathways in cybersecurity and technology.” Dr. Nitin Tandon, Vice Chancellor, CT University, said, “This collaboration is an important step towards strengthening our industry-aligned academic framework. By integrating specialised cybersecurity courses and internationally recognised certification pathways, we aim to ensure that our students gain relevant technical knowledge, practical exposure and the professional competencies required to succeed in a competitive global environment.” The collaboration was facilitated in the presence of Nitin Bhogan, Director, Quick Heal Academy, and Awadhesh Kumar Shukla, Manager, Quick Heal Academy, representing the industry partner. Dr. Pankaj Jain, Director – CRC, and Dr. Ishpreet Singh Virk, Head of Department – Computer Science and Engineering, School of Engineering and Technology (SOET), CT University, are also associated with the university’s broader focus on strengthening industry engagement, academic innovation and career-oriented learning. Through this partnership, CT University continues to reinforce its commitment to experiential education, industry–academia collaboration and the development of future-ready professionals equipped to address emerging challenges in cybersecurity and the digital technology sector. title: CT University Develops Smart SOS Safety Shoes with Hidden Emergency Alert Technology - CT University
text:
CT University Develops Smart SOS Safety Shoes with Hidden Emergency Alert Technology Monday, 05 October 2026 1 / 3 View Full Image Event Photo Gallery
                                    (3) About This Event Ludhiana: In a significant advancement towards technology-driven personal safety, the Robotics & Automation Lab of CT University has developed innovative Smart SOS Safety Shoes that can trigger an emergency alert through a simple, predefined foot movement. Designed for situations involving theft, threats or other emergencies, the technology provides an alternative SOS mechanism when accessing a mobile phone or manually activating an alert may not be possible. An integrated accelerometer detects the predefined motion and activates the SOS signal, which can then transmit an alert to a designated emergency response system. Smart Technology, Hidden in Every Step A key feature of the innovation is its discreet and user-friendly design. The electronic components are seamlessly integrated within the footwear, with no visible circuits, wires or bulky attachments, allowing the shoes to retain the appearance of everyday footwear while concealing their safety technology. The system also incorporates rechargeable electronics, enabling repeated use without frequent replacement of embedded components. Dr. Harmeet Singh said, “We have integrated an accelerometer into the shoes to detect a specific predefined motion, which triggers the SOS signal in an emergency situation. The Smart SOS Shoes were developed by our Robotics & Automation Lab within one week, demonstrating the potential for rapid innovation and practical implementation. With further refinement and testing, the technology has strong potential for commercialisation in the near future.” Innovation with a Purpose Commenting on the innovation, Pro Chancellor Dr. Manbeet Singh said, “At CT University, we believe that meaningful innovation is technology that addresses real-world challenges. The Smart SOS Safety Shoes are a remarkable example of how our students and faculty are transforming ideas into practical solutions with a strong focus on safety and social impact.” Vice Chancellor Dr. Nitin Tandon added, “This innovation reflects the spirit of research, experimentation and problem-solving that we strive to foster at CT University. Developing a functional safety solution within such a short timeframe demonstrates the creativity and technical potential of our Robotics & Automation Lab. We look forward to seeing this technology evolve further.” The Smart SOS Safety Shoes were developed and tested by the Robotics team comprising Er. Pulkit Sangar, Er. Dharmpreet Singh and Mr. Gurkirat Singh, who evaluated the system through real-life scenarios and under varied conditions. The innovation reflects CT University’s continued commitment to fostering practical research, emerging technologies and solutions that have the potential to create meaningful impact beyond the campus. title: CT University Develops Affordable Smart Trouser - CT University
text:

                                    (2) About This Event In a significant step towards practical and people-centric innovation, the Robotics Lab at CT University has developed a Smart Trouser designed to address common issues of lower back pain while helping users maintain the correct knee position during sitting. The innovative project was developed through a collaborative effort by the Robotics Team of CT University, School of Design & Innovation, and AIESEC student Ismail Ashraf from Egypt. The smart trouser integrates simple yet effective technology to provide comfort and support during prolonged sitting. The key feature of the Smart Trouser is a heating pad that provides warmth to the lower back, along with two vibrators designed to provide vibration-based stimulation to the lower back. The heating and vibration functions can be operated through two buttons incorporated at the front of the trouser as buckles. The device offers three different intensity modes for vibration, allowing users to adjust the experience according to their preference. The Robotics Team comprising Er. Pulkit Sangar, Er. Dharmpreet Singh and Gurkirat Singh successfully completed the project in just one week, with the entire prototype developed at a cost of less than ₹2,000, demonstrating that meaningful innovation can also be affordable and accessible. The idea was initially discussed with Gurdeep Singh from the School of Design & Innovation, who contributed to the project by suggesting and incorporating the heating pad feature, further strengthening the functionality of the prototype. Chancellor’s Comment S. Charanjit Singh Channi, Chancellor, CT University, said, “Innovation finds its true purpose when it solves real-life challenges. title: Bridge to Brilliance: Principals' Honor Conclave - CT University
text:

The event recognised and honoured more than 400 Principals for their dedicated service and leadership in the field of education. The gathering highlighted the crucial role of school Principals in nurturing young minds, developing future-ready students and creating a strong foundation for higher education and professional careers. Addressing the gathering, Vice Chancellor Dr. Nitin Tandon spoke about the University’s School Connect Program, an initiative aimed at bridging the gap between schools and universities. He emphasised the importance of establishing stronger academic linkages, enabling school students to gain greater exposure to higher education opportunities, emerging career pathways, industry-oriented learning and the evolving academic landscape. Dr. Tandon highlighted that meaningful collaboration between schools and universities can help students make informed career choices at the right stage and prepare them for the demands of the future. The conclave also featured an informative address by Admission Head Dr. Ashish Raina, who elaborated on the Hotel Management Pathway to Abroad. He highlighted the growing opportunities available in the hospitality sector and explained how students pursuing Hotel Management can explore international education, professional training and global career opportunities. Adding an experiential dimension to the conclave, various schools and academic departments of CT University showcased their projects and innovative work. The exhibits provided the visiting Principals with an insight into the University’s academic environment, practical learning approach, innovation-driven education and multidisciplinary programmes. He called for stronger collaboration between schools and universities to ensure that students receive the right guidance, exposure and opportunities to build successful careers. He stated that such platforms are important for creating a shared vision for the future of education, where institutions work together to identify the aspirations of students and provide them with pathways that connect learning with real-world opportunities. title: CT University Student Sneha Gharami to Represent India at Commonwealth Powerlifting Championship - CT University
text: CT University Student Sneha Gharami to Represent India at Commonwealth Powerlifting Championship Friday, 31 July 2026 View Full Image About This Event For many young athletes, representing India remains a distant dream. For Sneha Gharami, a second-year BA student at CT University, that dream has now become reality one built on years of sacrifice, unwavering determination, and the courage to overcome financial hardships. A resident of Howrah, West Bengal, Sneha has been selected to represent India in the Junior 76 kg category at the Commonwealth Powerlifting Championship 2026, to be held in Winnipeg, Canada, from September 17 to 27. Behind this remarkable achievement lies a story of resilience. Coming from a financially constrained background, Sneha faced numerous challenges in pursuing professional sports. Yet, she refused to let circumstances define her future. Her relentless dedication, coupled with the support of CT University’s Sports Scholarship Programme, enabled her to continue both her education and intensive training without giving up on her ambitions. Her selection came after an exceptional performance at the National Equipped Powerlifting Championship in Hyderabad, where she broke her own national record by lifting 222.5 kg in Squats, surpassing her previous best of 212.5 kg. She also won Gold Medals in Squat and Deadlift along with a Silver Medal in Bench Press, earning her place in the Indian contingent. Sneha’s journey has been marked by consistent excellence. She has previously won three Gold Medals at the Asian Equipped Powerlifting Championships, Overall Gold at the National Equipped Powerlifting Championship (Punjab, 2024), and Overall Gold at the Federation Cup Powerlifting Championship (Delhi, 2024). Today, her story stands as an inspiration for thousands of aspiring athletes who dare to dream despite limited resources. Congratulating Sneha, Pro Chancellor Dr. Manbir Singh said, “Sneha’s journey is far more than a sporting achievement—it is a story of perseverance, courage, and belief. Despite financial challenges, she never allowed her dreams to fade. At CT University, we are committed to ensuring that talented students receive the opportunities they deserve. Her selection to represent India fills the entire university with pride, and we are confident she will inspire countless young athletes across the country.” Director of Sports Gurdeep Singh said, “Sneha’s dedication has been exceptional from day one. Every record she has broken is the result of countless hours of discipline and hard work. We are proud to have witnessed her transformation into an international athlete and believe she will make India proud.” Director, Department of Student Welfare (DSW), Er. Davinder Singh, added, “Sneha’s success reflects the strength of CT University’s commitment to nurturing talent beyond classrooms. Her journey reminds every student that determination, when supported with the right opportunities, can overcome even the toughest circumstances.” As Sneha prepares to wear the Indian jersey on the international stage, her journey has become much more than a sporting success—it is a powerful reminder that dreams know no boundaries when determination meets opportunity. Her achievement adds yet another proud chapter to CT University’s growing legacy of producing champions who inspire the nation. Back to All Events
